items.title: Singapore's UOB misses on Q3 profit, margin pressures loom; shares slide
items.summary: SINGAPORE: United Overseas Bank (UOB) said on Wednesday its third-quarter net profit missed expectations and flagged further margin pressures ahead, sending its shares sliding. UOB Chief Financial Officer Leong Yung Chee said NIM for the full year is likely to fall below 1.75 per cent, down from the previous quarter's guidance of 1.75 per cent to 1.80 per cent. For the third quarter, the bank's NIM narrowed 6 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 1.68 per cent due to higher funding costs.

items.title: MACC remands three, including Datuk, over RM1mil cigarette smuggling bribes
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Three people, including a company owner with a Datuk title, have been remanded over allegations that they paid RM1 million in bribes to police officers to protect cigarette smuggling activities. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said the suspects were believed to have acted as intermediaries, channelling bribes to several policemen to ensure no enforcement action was taken against cigarette smuggling operations in the East Coast states and the Klang Valley. The suspects comprise a male company owner and two women, who work as a tuition teacher and a marketing officer.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM NOV 4, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher but retreated thereafter, tracking mixed performances across regional markets following overnight cues from Wall Street. The benchmark index opened 1.46 points higher at 1,623.31 before giving up its gains. In the crypto market, Bitcoin fell to RM313,518 due to broader market pressures.

items.title: SPNB seeks private sector partnerships to reduce RMR housing waiting lists
items.summary: Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said the initiative would involve government agencies, government-linked companies (GLCs) and private firms amid high demand for affordable housing. She said the proposed collaborations would help SPNB increase its construction capacity beyond the government's annual RM500 million funding ceiling. "Demand for RMR homes remains high, but the government's annual allocation is capped at RM500 million.

items.title: Princeton Digital secures RM5.1bil funding for Johor expansion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Princeton Digital Group has secured US$1.3 billion (RM5.1 billion) in green financing to support the continued development and expansion of its JH1 data centre campus in Johor. The facility is structured under Princeton Digital's Green Finance Framework and supports the development of JH1 in line with recognised green building standards. The campus obtained Green Building Index Gold certification for design and LEED Gold certification for operations.

items.title: Report: Najib will pay RM50m fine today to unlock house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is reportedly set to pay his RM50 million fine today, satisfying the core condition required to transfer him from Kajang Prison to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. The fine forms part of Najib's conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million from SRC International Sdn Bhd. The Kuala Lumpur High Court originally sentenced him in July 2020 to 12 years’ imprisonment and a RM210 million fine, penalties that were upheld by the Federal Court in August 2022.

items.title: New Zealand votes with economy, cost of living in focus
items.summary: WELLINGTON: New Zealanders are voting this week in an election focused on rising costs of living and the economy, as pollsters forecast a tight contest and neither main party close to winning a majority. But the opposition Labour Party is banking that voter worries about costs of living will see it returned to office. - The cost of living is the biggest issue for voters, according to the RNZ-Reid Research Poll run by New Zealand's public broadcaster.

items.title: CGS International positive on Oriental Kopi's store roll-out in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CGS International Securities Malaysia Sdn Bhd remains constructive on Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd's store roll-out as the group is on track to reach 40-41 Malaysian outlets by the end of 2026, up from 34 outlets as at July this year. The brokerage said that with six mall locations already secured, Oriental Kopi's target of eight to 10 new outlets per annum looked achievable. Meanwhile, CGS International hosted Oriental Kopi's management and investors on Nov 3, 2026, to discuss its Oct 2026 menu language controversy.

items.title: Clear project purpose, investment readiness vital in viable regional connections
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Clear project objectives, investment readiness and commercial viability will be critical to translating Asean's renewable energy potential into viable cross-border electricity connections, says Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB). Hasmarizal Hassan, said regional interconnection projects must be supported by comprehensive feasibility studies, appropriate technology, committed electricity buyers and clearly defined investment decision points to ensure their long-term sustainability. at the Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW) 2026.

items.title: Stocks and dollar drop as Democrats enjoy big early wins
items.summary: HONG KONG: Asian stocks fell with the dollar Wednesday, with the Democrats enjoying big early gains in the US midterms as they look to take control of both houses of Congress, which analysts said could lead to gridlock on Capitol Hill. A Democrat win would deal a hefty blow to Trump's agenda for his final two years in the White House, and analysts warned it would likely mean very little gets done in Washington in that time. "A narrow blue wave may be largely priced in," said Chris Weston at Pepperstone.

items.title: No instructions from Najib to settle RM50mil fine, says lawyer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's lawyer, Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee, said he had received no instructions from his client to pay the RM50 million fine, which would allow him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. Farhan's presence at the Kuala Lumpur courts complex had fuelled speculation that the fine would be settled. I have not received any instructions regarding the fine.

items.title: Gold firms on softer oil prices, US midterm results awaited
items.summary: BENGALURU: Gold prices edged higher in early Asian trade on Wednesday as softer oil prices eased inflation concerns, while investors awaited US midterm election results and key labour market data for clues on the Federal Reserve's monetary policy direction. Spot gold rose 0.2 per cent to US$3,934.75 an ounce by 12.24am GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.1 per cent to US$3,943.20. Among other precious metals, spot silver fell 0.2 per cent to US$49.67 an ounce, while platinum rose 0.3 per cent to US$1,422.15 and palladium gained 0.5 per cent to US$938.49.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Malaysia seeks wider use of local currencies in cross-border trade through BRICS cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Malaysia aims to enhance the use of local currencies in cross-border trade and investment transactions through BRICS cooperation, thereby reducing transaction costs and foreign exchange risks. It said wider use of local currencies could improve the efficiency of foreign exchange exposure management and support the development of regional foreign exchange markets. “An increase in transactions using regional currencies, including those of BRICS member countries, could also enhance liquidity and support the development of regional foreign exchange markets, thereby providing businesses with more options,” the ministry stated to the Dewan Rakyat.

items.title: Drop beer sponsor or lose permit, sports ministry warns Hyrox Kuala Lumpur organisers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The Youth and Sports Ministry has threatened to withhold event approval for the upcoming Hyrox Kuala Lumpur 2026 fitness race unless organisers completely cut ties with an alcoholic beverage sponsor. The ministry issued the ultimatum following public scrutiny over a viral promotional graphic naming a commercial beer brand as the event’s “Official Beer Partner”. Organisers were also reminded that staging an event without official sanction violates Section 36(1) of the Sports Development Act 1997, which bars companies from managing sports events without a licence issued by the Commissioner of Sports Malaysia.

items.title: Da'i Syed's final appeal against rape conviction to be decided today
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal here is scheduled to deliver its decision today on celebrity preacher Da'i Syed's final appeal to set aside his conviction and 10-year prison sentence and three strokes of the cane for rape. The three-member panel, chaired by Datuk Azman Abdullah, is scheduled to sit with Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid to hear the final appeal by Da'i Syed, whose real name is Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohd Shaiful, 31. Syed Shah Iqmal, dressed in a white robe and accompanied by his wife, Hana Ismail, arrived at the court at 8.55am.

items.title: China's services growth slows to three-month low as confidence weakens
items.summary: BEIJING: China's services activity in October expanded at its slowest pace since July, with business confidence easing as firms grappled with fierce competition and rising costs, a private-sector survey showed on Wednesday. New export business rose for the sixth straight month, extending the longest growth streak seen since 2024. Business confidence slipped to its lowest since July, with firms citing concerns over rising input prices and heightened competition.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia opens higher but reverses early gains amid cautious sentiment
items.summary: At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) decreased 3.13 points to 1,618.72 from yesterday's close of 1,621.85. The benchmark index opened 1.46 points higher at 1,623.31. In active trade, Aizo rose one sen to eight sen, Dagang Nexchange, Bina Puri and Zetrix AI inched up half a sen each to 41 sen, 22 sen and 6.5 sen, respectively.

items.title: New Zealand jobless rate hits 11-year high in run-up to polls
items.summary: The jobless rate rose to 5.7 per cent in the three months to September, its highest since 2015, from 5.5 per cent in the previous quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday. Employment fell 0.1 per cent from the prior quarter. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand had also forecast a 5.5 per cent jobless rate.

items.title: Orkim's early vessel delivery to drive earnings growth: analysts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Orkim Bhd has taken delivery of its 21st vessel, MT Orkim Jade, ahead of schedule, a development expected to bring forward its earnings contribution and strengthen revenue visibility, according to RHB Research. The 2026-built clean petroleum products tanker has a carrying capacity of 14,500 deadweight tonnes (DWT), lifting Orkim's total fleet capacity by 5.4 per cent to 281,534 DWT. Orkim remains on track to dispose of Orkim Fortune in the second half of 2026, which would bring its fleet capacity to about 274,200 DWT by year-end, followed by the expected delivery of Orkim Ruby in 2027.

items.title: Kerjaya Prospek set to ride power infrastructure boom
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd is poised to benefit from robust project flows in the power infrastructure segment, according to Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB). HLIB said the contract brings Kerjaya Prospek's outstanding order book to about RM6 billion and year-to-date job replenishment to RM3.5 billion, providing strong earnings visibility alongside a healthy tender pipeline of about RM2 billion. On valuation, HLIB said Kerjaya Prospek trades at 13.8 times and 12.6 times its forecast financial year 2027 and 2028 earnings, respectively, below its three-year historical average of 14.3 times and the peer average of 18.8 times and 16.5 times.

items.title: Oil edges down as investors await US midterm election results
items.summary: BEIJING: Oil prices slipped in early trade on Wednesday as investors awaited the results of the US midterm elections and their potential impact on peace talks in the Middle East, even as industry data showed US crude inventories unexpectedly fell last week. Brent crude futures fell 26 cents, or 0.25 per cent, to US$103.34 a barrel by 1.57am GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 53 cents, or 0.55 per cent, to US$95.56.

items.title: Overlapping jurisdictions hamper monitoring of halal slaughterhouses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Overlapping jurisdictions among government ministries, departments and agencies have made it difficult to monitor slaughterhouse operations and enforce halal certification compliance, potentially allowing breaches of Islamic requirements. Religious authorities, including state Islamic religious departments and the Malaysian Islamic Development Department (Jakim), oversee compliance with Islamic requirements, halal certification and enforcement relating to halal status. Jakim said slaughterhouse operations fell under the jurisdiction of several authorities because they involved various processes, including slaughtering, hygiene, food safety, halal certification compliance and premises licensing.

items.title: Foreign AI election interference claims under Online Safety Act probe, ministry tells Parliament
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The federal government will deploy existing communications and cyber safety laws to counter an alleged foreign-linked artificial intelligence influence campaign targeting Malaysian electorates, while drafting a dedicated AI Governance Bill to establish regulatory oversight over developers, the Communications Ministry told Parliament. The ministry disclosed this in a written parliamentary reply yesterday to Pasir Mas MP Tuan Haji Ahmad Fadhli Shaari, who questioned what steps the government would take to investigate foreign election meddling conducted through generative AI platforms, including Claude. The ministry confirmed that the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is treating the allegations seriously and has sought detailed technical clarification and supporting evidence from Anthropic, the US-based creator of Claude, to ensure any regulatory assessment is grounded in empirical findings.

items.title: Suhakam to meet Perak govt over monastery demolition dispute
items.summary: IPOH: The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) will meet the Perak government over alleged human rights violations linked to a threat to demolish the Sakyamuni Cave Monastery in Gunung Kanthan here for quarrying activities. Suhakam commissioner Abdul Kadir Jailani Ismail said the move followed a memorandum submitted by the monastery's monks on Aug 27, alleging restricted access and intimidation, including surveillance by drones. "Suhakam is mandated to provide views and advice to state governments on human rights issues.

items.title: Najib to pay RM50mil fine today for house arrest release
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak is reportedly set to pay the RM50 million fine imposed on him to enable him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. A source said the fine would be paid by a representative of Najib at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex today. Najib, 73, was sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million after being found guilty by the Kuala Lumpur High Court on July 28, 2020, on seven charges involving the misappropriation of RM42 million in funds belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Woman arrested over alleged harassment of visitors at Kuala Lumpur shopping mall
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Police detained a woman yesterday to assist in investigations into an incident involving the harassment of visitors at a shopping mall in the capital. Dang Wangi District Police Chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said police detained the 25-year-old woman at 5.40 pm in Bandar Sri Damansara. He urged members of the public with information about the incident to contact the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2146 0522 or 03-2146 0585, the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters Control Centre at 03-2600 2222, or visit the nearest police station.

items.title: Two men killed, woman injured in separate Penang road crashes
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Two men died and a woman injured in two separate road crashes in Penang between late Tuesday night and early Wednesday morning. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said eight personnel from the Bayan Baru fire station were deployed to the scene after receiving an emergency call. "Upon arrival, rescuers found two victims from the motorcycle.

items.title: As data centre power share heads for 21pc, Putrajaya moves to avoid ‘phantom demand’ hogging Malaysia’s grid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Data centre operators seeking grid connection in Peninsular Malaysia must now submit 10-year staggered energy projection plans and execute binding commercial pacts with Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), as the federal government clamps down on speculative developers hoarding power capacity. Official data highlights a widening disconnect between contracted grid allocations and real-world utilization. As of August 2026, contracted data centre capacity stood at 2,346 megawatts (MW), yet active facilities were drawing only 1,374 MW, representing 58.6 per cent of contracted volumes.

items.title: Malaysia ensures food, water and legal assistance for 130 citizens detained in Pakistan over cyber-scam links
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The government is monitoring the welfare of 130 Malaysians detained by Pakistani authorities over suspected links to a cyber-scam syndicate, ensuring that they have access to food, water and legal assistance. Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni said Malaysian diplomatic representatives in every country were responsible for ensuring that Malaysians facing difficulties or detained by local authorities received appropriate attention, particularly in terms of their welfare and necessary assistance. Meanwhile, Lukanisman said the government was in the final stages of preparing the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) card to register refugees under a module developed by Malaysia, in line with the government’s position that the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) should cease its refugee registration activities.

items.title: Sabah offers to host Malaysia's proposed nuclear energy hub
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah is prepared to be considered as a potential hub for Malaysia's proposed nuclear energy programme, said State Government Backbenchers Club (BBC) chairman Datuk Masiung Banah. He said the state needed to prepare for rising electricity demand by 2031, while reducing its reliance on natural gas and diesel amid volatile global energy markets. Masiung said Sabah's electricity supply capacity remained strained and lagged behind the development of utilities in Peninsular Malaysia.

items.title: Yuneswaran: Deepavali expo boosts small traders while promoting racial unity through cultural celebrations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Large-scale business expos such as the 24th Deepavali Carnival (DC26) not only strengthen the economic prospects of local entrepreneurs and small traders, but also promote racial unity through cross-cultural integration. Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said the Deepavali expo attracted people from diverse backgrounds, including visitors of different ethnicities and foreign tourists, who came together to celebrate Malaysia’s cultural diversity. “The expo goes beyond business activities to include cultural programmes organised by the Indian community, helping to foster greater unity among the people.

items.title: Malaysia's first female Education director-general Asiah Abu Samah dies at 89
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Sri Asiah Abu Samah, the country's first female Education director-general, died at KPJ Damansara Hospital at 5am today. Asiah made history when she became the first woman appointed Education director-general on Nov 27, 1991. She was appointed Deputy Education director-general II before being promoted to Deputy Education director-general I in mid-1990.

items.title: OPR hike to boost bank earnings, deposit rivalry a concern
items.summary: However, intensifying deposit competition could limit the benefits, says Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB). Its sensitivity analysis showed that Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd could record the largest improvement of 6.2 basis points, followed by Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd and Public Bank Bhd at 5.8 basis points each. RHB Bank Bhd was expected to see a 5.5-basis-point uplift, followed by Affin Bank Bhd at 5.1 basis points and AmBank (M) Bhd at 4.7 basis points.

items.title: Flash floods shut NKVE, Elite, GCE stretches around Shah Alam [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Heavy overnight rain triggered flash floods along several major stretches around Shah Alam early this morning, forcing road closures on the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE), North-South Expressway Central Link (Elite), and Guthrie Corridor Expressway (GCE). Highway concessionaire Plus Malaysia Bhd, in an update on X, said flash floods hit Km9.1 of the NKVE between Shah Alam and Subang at 4.07am. Traffic from Seafield heading towards Shah Alam was temporarily diverted to the Shah Alam Toll Plaza.

items.title: Man dies after parang attack in Teluk Intan
items.summary: TELUK INTAN: A man died after being attacked with parangs by three men outside a shop in Taman Banjar Jaya here yesterday afternoon. Hilir Perak police chief Assistant Commissioner Chua Kok Lian said the victim died while receiving treatment at Teluk Intan Hospital following the 3.53pm incident. "Initial investigations found that the victim was attacked by three men armed with parangs.

items.title: Penang tightens fireworks sales rules ahead of 2027 Chinese New Year
items.summary: In a statement, MBPP said applications for the 2027 Chinese New Year Seasonal Temporary Stall Licence are open from today until Dec 31, while applications for the Seasonal Temporary Stall Licence for Fireworks Sales are open from today until Nov 30. "The Seasonal Temporary Stall Licence and the Fireworks Sales Licence are two separate licences, and approval of a temporary stall licence does not automatically allow traders to sell fireworks. "Traders intending to sell fireworks must obtain separate approval and permits from the police," MBPP said.

items.title: Govt agencies ordered to strengthen readiness against cyber, supply threats
items.summary: Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said the move was part of efforts to strengthen national security preparedness amid global uncertainty and geopolitical conflicts that could trigger various threats. He said national security risk assessments must now take into account non-conventional threats, including cyberattacks, sabotage, disinformation and supply chain disruptions. Shamsul Azri said national sovereignty and security would not be compromised, with the government giving serious attention to risks that could affect national security, strategic sector interests and public safety.

items.title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning issued for eight states until 10am
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain, and strong wind warning for eight states until 10am today. The weather warning affects Kedah (Kulim and Bandar Baharu) and Penang (Seberang Perai Selatan, Seberang Perai Tengah, Barat Daya, and Timor Laut). Similar conditions are forecast in Perak (Kampar, Kinta, Kuala Kangsar, Bagan Datuk, Hulu Perak, Kerian, Larut Matang, Selama, Manjung, Perak Tengah, and Hilir Perak), Kelantan (Gua Musang), and Terengganu (Kemaman and Dungun).

items.title: Flooding shuts key Shah Alam expressway links, diversions active on NKVE and ELITE
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 4 — Pre-dawn flash floods forced the emergency closure of critical sections along the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) and the North-South Expressway Central Link (ELITE) near Shah Alam today, crippling morning peak-hour commutes across the central Klang Valley. Access from the Guthrie Corridor Expressway (GCE) towards the Shah Alam Toll Plaza also remained impassable this morning. However, traffic conditions saw partial relief after all lanes at the Shah Alam interchange along the ELITE highway, heading from Seafield towards Setia Alam, were reopened to traffic at 6.43am under cautious driving advisories.

items.title: Man slashed to death by three machete-wielding attackers in Teluk Intan, woman detained
items.summary: TELUK INTAN, Nov 4 — A man died after being ambushed and slashed by three machete-wielding assailants outside a shop here yesterday afternoon, prompting police to arrest a 27-year-old local woman to assist in a murder investigation. Hilir Perak district police headquarters dispatched officers to the scene after receiving an emergency 999 call from a member of the public at 3.53pm on Tuesday reporting a violent assault in progress in front of a shophouse. Members of the public with relevant information are urged to contact the Hilir Perak district police headquarters at 05-629 9222 or visit the nearest police station.

items.title: Anwar moved by 1982 photograph showing late supporter celebrating his first election victory
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was deeply moved upon receiving an old photograph from a student from Alor Setar, Kedah, which captured him celebrating his first electoral victory for the Permatang Pauh parliamentary seat in 1982. In a Facebook post, the Prime Minister shared that the photograph was presented by Zahra Mohamad Zelman, who approached him accompanied by her friends from Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Sultanah Asma at the Parliament building yesterday. Anwar noted that the image captured a moment when he was being celebrated by Zahra’s great-grandfather, the late Arshad Ahmad, following his win in the Permatang Pauh constituency.

items.title: PTPTN first class honours loan exemption under review as govt weighs fairness and sustainability
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 —The government will study a loan repayment exemption policy for previous National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers who earned first-class honours degrees. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the review would consider fairness to borrowers while ensuring the country’s education financing policy remains sustainable. Chong said previous loan agreements explicitly provided for repayment exemptions for borrowers who graduated with first-class honours degrees, and urged the government to maintain the exemption for existing borrowers until a new policy is announced.

items.title: Sabah Pakatan chief condemns use of religious sentiment in political debate over parliamentary agreement
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 4 — Sabah Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud has reminded political parties not to exploit religious sentiment as a weapon to challenge opponents’ strategies, following remarks linking parliamentary democracy as an institution to an end-times figure. The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs) expressed regret over a statement by PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang, who was alleged to have likened the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) approach to “Dajjal” (literally the Deceitful Messiah), stressing that such a label was highly unfamiliar and could confuse Muslims in Sabah. The CSA can be debated rationally within the framework of parliamentary democracy without resorting to religious sentiment to discredit those with differing views,” he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: National security, UUCA repeal and misleading ‘badal haj’ ads among key issues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Issues concerning national security amid rising military tensions in the Asia-Pacific region, the future governance of universities following the repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA) and efforts to tackle misleading advertisements for badal haj services are among the matters to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper on Parliament’s official website, William Leong Jee Keen (PH-Selayang) will ask the Defence Minister during the Questions for Oral Answers session about the government’s stance on rising tensions and military escalation in the Asia-Pacific region, particularly measures to safeguard national security and maintain stability within Asean. The Dewan Rakyat sitting runs for 37 days until Dec 8.

items.title: Save your tears (for the traffic): 130,000 The Weeknd fans set to gridlock Bukit Jalil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Motorists and commuters heading towards Bukit Jalil face severe traffic gridlock this evening and tomorrow as Canadian superstar The Weeknd takes the stage at the National Stadium for the two-night finale of his global tour. Commuters transferring to the LRT Ampang Line or the MRT Putrajaya Line must depart Bukit Jalil by midnight. An earlier 11.30pm departure deadline applies to fans heading towards the LRT Kelana Jaya Line, the KL Monorail, or the MRT Kajang Line.

items.title: Working or retired? Here is what Budget 2027 offers Malaysians over 60
items.summary: Depending on your circumstances, Budget 2027 packs a variety of measures that impact older Malaysians differently. Cash aid through STR and SARA Budget 2027 increases the combined allocation for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to a massive RM16 billion. Higher individual income tax relief and lower rates For older Malaysians still earning an income, the government plans to increase individual income tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000 starting from Year of Assessment 2027.

items.title: Private universities steal the spotlight as Malaysia sets a historic record in QS Asia 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — More than 50 Malaysian universities penetrated the QS World University Rankings Asia 2027 for the first time, with 11 emerging among the top 100 in Asia. They include Sunway University, INTI International University, Asia Pacific University of Technology and Innovation (APU), SEGi University, IMU University, MILA University, Tunku Abdul Rahman University of Management and Technology, Perdana University, Quest International University (QIU), Nilai University, UNITAR International University and Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah (UniSHAMS). Sunway University also ranked among the top 50 for the first time while INTI International University made it into the top 100 for the first time.

items.title: Hafidz Othman appointed new Prisons Department chief, takes office on Nov 5
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — Deputy Commissioner General of Prisons (Community) Hafidz Othman has been appointed the new Commissioner General of Prisons, effective Nov 5, the Prisons Department said. In a statement today, the department said Hafidz received his appointment letter from Public Service director-general Tan Sri Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz. He also served as Deputy Commissioner General of Prisons (Management) in 2025.

items.title: Govt pays RM20.27b in income tax refunds to 3.65m taxpayer cases as at Oct 31
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — A total of RM20.271 billion in income tax refunds involving 3.65 million taxpayer cases had been paid as at Oct 31, 2026. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said of the total, RM6.84 billion had been refunded to 3.4 million individual taxpayers, while RM13.036 billion had been refunded to 206,234 corporate taxpayers, including micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Amir Hamzah reiterated the government’s commitment to addressing the backlog of excess income tax refunds to ensure that all outstanding payments are made promptly.

items.title: Johor identifies 337 flood hotspots as state braces for northeast monsoon
items.summary: He said the relevant projects included Phase 1 of the Sungai Johor Flood Mitigation Plan, the Sungai Pemandi Flood Mitigation Plan and a flood alleviation project in Kampung Sungai Kapal Lama in Pengerang. In Batu Pahat, Mohamad Fazli said the DID had identified 41 flood hotspots, while the JKR had detected 21 high-risk locations along federal and state roads, covering a total distance of 6.5 kilometres. In Segamat, Mohamad Fazli said the DID had identified 29 flood hotspots, while the JKR had identified 16 high-risk locations, comprising eight federal roads and eight state roads.

items.title: After Customs flags import irregularities, maritime expert asks MACC to revisit RM220m crude cargo report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — A maritime industry executive today asked whether the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) would take further action on his report over alleged discrepancies in petroleum cargo records, following the Royal Malaysian Customs Department’s latest disclosure on import declaration irregularities. Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan lodged the report on June 5 over alleged discrepancies between bills of lading and the physical movement of petroleum cargo at Tanjung Langsat Port, Johor, in transactions reportedly worth millions of ringgit. Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of experience in the maritime industry, questioned whether the latest information from Customs could give MACC grounds to revisit the concerns raised in his report.

items.title: New law replacing AUKU will not curtail students’ freedom of expression, says Zahid
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 3 — The new Bill to replace the now-repealed Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) will not affect students’ freedom of expression, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. He said the Cabinet agreed that the proposed legislation would be limited to matters concerning university administration, including academic affairs, governance and the appointment of senate members, Ahmad Zahid also said that the new law would also cover the selection of university management personnel, including vice-chancellors and deputy vice-chancellors. “Under AUKU, universities did take action against students.

items.title: Govt approves over RM250m for ECRL expansion plans and new Kota Bharu bus terminal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — The Madani government has approved more than RM250 million to strengthen the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) development in Kelantan, according to the Ministry of Finance (MOF). This includes building a new bus terminal at the Kota Bharu ECRL Station and preliminary works for a proposed extension to Rantau Panjang, said the ministry in a statement today. Of the total, RM30 million has been allocated for the new bus terminal, while more than RM200 million will fund preliminary works for the proposed ECRL extension from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang.

items.title: Fashion Valet trial: Investment funds cannot be used to pay dividends, court told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Sessions Court hearing the case involving Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd (Fashion Valet) founders Datin Vivy Sofinas Yusof and her husband, Datuk Fadzarudin Shah Anuar, was told today that investment funds could not be used to pay dividends to any party, including the company’s shareholders. Corporate lawyer Anne Wong Wai Yee, 49, who was involved in drafting the shareholders’ agreement between the couple and seven other companies, including Fashion Valet, on March 5, 2018, said the agreement did not contain any provision allowing investment funds to be used for such payments. Capital Sdn Bhd, Transasia E-Commerce Inc., Start Today Co. Ltd., Reussi Sdn Bhd and Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Traders risk RM100,000 fine for hidden charges, Parliament told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Traders who impose hidden charges or disclose additional fees only at the final stage of a transaction may face legal action, including fines of up to RM100,000, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. He said the practice misled consumers and undermined their right to know the actual price before making a purchase. Armizan said Section 10B(1) of the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011 [Act 723] allows action against businesses that fail to include all taxes, duties, and other charges in the prices of goods or services they display, advertise, publish, or quote.

items.title: Mount Kinabalu training centre faces calls to halt work over indigenous, environmental concerns
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 3 — The ongoing construction of a high-altitude training centre on Mount Kinabalu has come under scrutiny, with indigenous groups and tourism stakeholders questioning its environmental impact, approvals and whether communities with customary ties to the mountain were adequately consulted. Bundu Tuhan Village Heritage and Culture head Adrian Soros also questioned whether communities with customary ties to the mountain had been consulted, saying many villagers were unaware of the construction. He said the project had obtained approval from the Sabah Parks Board of Trustees and endorsement from the Mount Kinabalu Native Customary Advisory Council.

items.title: Zahid denies trying to sabotage govt, says he has documents on cancelled rural projects
items.summary: JASIN, Nov 3 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied allegations that he intended to sabotage the Madani Government by revealing the cancellation or postponement of rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, maintained that his remarks concerning the suspension or cancellation of Letters of Acceptance (SSTs) for the projects were factual, adding that he was prepared to produce official documents to substantiate his claims. Yesterday, Jelutong MP RSN Rayer, while interjecting during a debate in the Dewan Rakyat, questioned Ahmad Zahid’s statement concerning the cancellation of rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak.

items.title: KL steps up drainage checks ahead of rainy season to prevent flash floods, says Hannah Yeoh
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — Spot checks on drainage systems and cleaning works in Kuala Lumpur are being stepped up to keep drains clear and reduce the risk of flash floods, especially during the rainy season. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said these checks must be carried out thoroughly, including during the dry season, to ensure cleaning works are done properly and drainage systems function well. Hannah said each parliamentary branch office has also activated teams to conduct patrols and channel the latest reports on flash flood-prone areas to the Kuala Lumpur mayor.

items.title: MCMC opens probe into Facebook post allegedly insulting Sultan of Selangor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has reportedly opened an investigation into a Facebook post suspected of containing highly offensive remarks against the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah. According to Bernama , MCMC said in a statement today that the post was also suspected of touching on sensitivities involving race, religion and royalty (3R). MCMC said it viewed seriously the spread of online content suspected of containing false information or insults against the royal institution, particularly material that could undermine social harmony.

items.title: Flood-hit Selangor districts back in firing line as MetMalaysia warns of torrential evening rain across 10 states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an evening thunderstorm warning across large swathes of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak until 8.00pm today, a day after torrential downpours triggered widespread flash floods across the Klang Valley. Perak faces widespread disruption spanning 12 districts, including Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Muallim, Batang Padang, Larut Matang, Selama, Kerian, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, and Bagan Datuk. Across Selangor, the advisory covers Hulu Selangor, Sabak Bernam, and Kuala Selangor, alongside Petaling and Klang, two major urban districts where drainage systems were inundated during Monday’s deluge.
